content.user_title: Build and Refine Interfaces with Uizze
content.value_statement: Interface changes can lose visual consistency or disrupt existing workflows. This skill guides implementation from visual targets and project conventions, with optional Uizze resources and explicit verification.
actual_capabilities: Guide inspection of existing screens, components, design tokens, assets, and data contracts before interface changes.
Use a supplied visual target or request a straight-on UI image when the host provides image generation.
Guide implementation of layouts, controls, and applicable loading, empty, error, and success states without inventing backend behavior.
Direct screenshot comparison, responsive checks, keyboard navigation checks, and correction of observed visual differences.
Search optional Uizze references and design packs through an authenticated MCP connection, with user selection before pack retrieval.
Guide integration of returned fonts, icons, and animation assets while checking checksums, license notices, and reduced-motion fallbacks.
limitations: Connected Uizze resources require an authenticated account with paid access; local interface work does not.
Image generation and screenshot capture depend on host tools; unavailable rendering leaves visual matching unverified.
Reference screens are not downloadable component code, and design pack font names do not grant font files or licenses.
The skill supplies workflow instructions, not a bundled renderer, backend implementation, or guaranteed haptics integration.

use_cases.title: Refine an Existing Product Screen
use_cases.description: Improve hierarchy, spacing, typography, and interface states while preserving existing components and application behavior.

use_cases.title: Implement an Approved Design
use_cases.description: Translate an approved screen image into working components and compare the rendered result against the target.
use_cases.target_user: Product designers working with coding agents

use_cases.title: Explore a Prototype Direction
use_cases.description: Develop a coherent prototype using existing project assets and optional Uizze examples, design packs, fonts, or icons.

prompt_templates.title: Improve One Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve the spacing and hierarchy of [screen]. Reuse existing components, preserve behavior, and report the checks you complete.

prompt_templates.title: Build from a Visual Target
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the supplied image for [screen] at [viewport]. Use our stack and real controls. Compare screenshots and report remaining differences.

prompt_templates.title: Select Uizze Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my authenticated Uizze connection to find two relevant references and a design pack for [screen]. Ask before retrieving the selected pack.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Verified Interface Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign [screen] using an approved visual target. Preserve data contracts, cover interface states, check keyboard access and responsive layouts, and document verification gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: a complete implementation and verification workflow

output_examples.input: Improve a settings screen using existing components without connecting to Uizze.
output: Change summary: related settings grouped together, labels clarified, and spacing aligned with existing tokens.
Behavior review: existing save actions and data contracts preserved.
Verification report: completed keyboard and viewport checks listed; unavailable checks marked as unverified.

output_examples.input: Implement an approved checkout image and compare the result at its original viewport.
output: Implementation summary: target layout translated into real text, components, and working controls.
Comparison report: target dimensions, rendered screenshot, and remaining visual differences documented.
Resource notes: missing fonts or imagery identified without claiming an exact match.

output_examples.input: Find Uizze references and suitable icon assets for a mobile onboarding screen.
output: Reference shortlist: up to three relevant examples, each with its returned image and Uizze source link.
Asset notes: available icon files, checksum checks, and material-specific license requirements.
Access limitation: unavailable authenticated resources reported without fabricated search results.

best_practices: Provide the target screen, real content, viewport dimensions, and existing behavior before requesting changes.
Approve the visual target and design pack selection before implementation or replacing existing design documents.
Use non-sensitive image prompts, preserve asset licenses, and require reports of actual visual and interaction checks.
anti_patterns: Do not copy another product's branding or screenshots directly into the application.
Do not treat reference images as backend specifications or flatten a complete screen into a background.
Do not expose credentials or signed URLs, bypass authorization, or claim verification when the required tools are unavailable.

faq.question: Do I need a Uizze account?
faq.answer: No account is needed for local interface work. Connected Uizze resources require authenticated paid access.

faq.question: Which coding assistants are supported?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available image generation, rendering, and MCP tools depend on the host.

faq.question: What happens when image generation is unavailable?
faq.answer: The workflow uses a supplied image. Without one, it builds from the brief and existing conventions without claiming an exact visual match.

faq.question: Does Uizze supply component code for reference screens?
faq.answer: No. Reference screens guide layouts and states, but they are not downloadable component code.

faq.question: Are all fonts and assets covered by the skill license?
faq.answer: No. Asset rights differ by material. Pack font names do not grant files or licenses, and supplied license notices must be preserved.

faq.question: How does the workflow verify interface changes?
faq.answer: It requests screenshot comparisons, relevant viewport checks, and keyboard checks. Unavailable rendering or unchecked behavior must be reported as unverified.
